messages.content:
You turn an incident review, written by a data-centre operator's own engineers after they solved a problem, into proposed changes to an "intelligence pill": a governed card of know-how that a facility team applies during the first hour of a cooling or power event.

You work only from the numbered sentences you are given. You add nothing from general knowledge.

Each change is one of:
- add_rule: a new piece of judgement. "when" = observable conditions a duty team could check; "then" = concrete actions; "why" = the reason the review gives; optional "escalate" = who must be called and on what trigger.
- amend_rule: add conditions or actions to an existing rule (give its rule_id) because this review sharpens it.
- add_guardrail: something the team or an assistant must not do or must not rely on.
- ask_expert: a question the review leaves open that an expert must answer before the pill can be trusted on it (for example a threshold, a time limit, who decides). Use this instead of guessing.

Hard rules:
1. Every add_rule, amend_rule and add_guardrail lists "evidence": the ids of the sentences that support it. No evidence, no change.
2. Never write a number (temperature, minutes, counts) that is not in a cited sentence. If a number matters but is missing, use ask_expert.
3. Write rules about facility operations (power, cooling, staffing, procedures, controls). Ignore cloud-software recovery details.
4. Prefer judgement over description: what an experienced engineer would check or do next, and why, not a retelling of the event.
5. If "focus_findings" are given, they are what the current pill failed to anticipate in this incident; make sure each one is either covered by a change or turned into ask_expert.

Reply with JSON only: {"changes": [ ... ]}. Shapes:

{"op":"add_guardrail","text":"...","evidence":["SRC:S1"]}

{"incident":{"id":"AZ-AUE-2023","title":"Utility voltage sag trips chillers; restart window closes as chilled-water loop heats (Azure Australia East, Sydney)","operator":"Microsoft Azure","site":"Australia East region, one Availability Zone, two adjacent data halls (Sydney)"},"review_sentences":[{"id":"AZ-AUE-2023:S6","text":"This incident was triggered by a utility power sag at 08:41 UTC on 30 August 2023, which impacted one of the three Availability Zones of the Australia East region."},{"id":"AZ-AUE-2023:S7","text":"This power sag tripped a subset of the cooling system chiller units offline and, while working to restore cooling, temperatures in the datacenter increased to levels above operational thresholds."},{"id":"AZ-AUE-2023:S12","text":"Starting at approximately 08:41 UTC on 30 August 2023, a utility voltage sag was caused by a lightning strike on electrical infrastructure approximately 18 miles from the impacted Availability Zone of the Australia East region."},{"id":"AZ-AUE-2023:S13","text":"The voltage sag caused cooling system chillers for multiple datacenters to shut down."},{"id":"AZ-AUE-2023:S14","text":"While some chillers automatically restarted, 13 failed to restart and required manual intervention."},{"id":"AZ-AUE-2023:S15","text":"To do so, the onsite team accessed the datacenter rooftop facilities, where the chillers are located, and proceeded to sequentially restart chillers moving from one datacenter to the next."},{"id":"AZ-AUE-2023:S16","text":"By the time the team reached the final five chillers requiring a manual restart, the water inside the pump system for these chillers (chilled water loop) had reached temperatures that were too high to allow them to be restarted."},{"id":"AZ-AUE-2023:S17","text":"In this scenario, the restart is inhibited by a self-protection mechanism that acts to prevent damage to the chiller that would occur by processing water at the elevated temperatures."},{"id":"AZ-AUE-2023:S18","text":"The five chillers that could not be restarted supported cooling for the two adjacent data halls which were impacted in this incident."},{"id":"AZ-AUE-2023:S19","text":"The two impacted data halls require at least four chillers to be operational."},{"id":"AZ-AUE-2023:S20","text":"Before the voltage sag, our cooling capacity for these halls consisted of seven chillers, with five chillers in operation and two chillers in standby."},{"id":"AZ-AUE-2023:S21","text":"At 10:30 UTC some networking, compute, and storage infrastructure began to shutdown automatically as data hall temperatures increased, impacting service availability."},{"id":"AZ-AUE-2023:S22","text":"At 11:34 UTC, as temperatures continued to increase, our onsite datacenter team began a remote shutdown of remaining networking, compute, and storage infrastructure in the impacted data halls to protect data durability, infrastructure health, and address the thermal runaway."},{"id":"AZ-AUE-2023:S23","text":"This shutdown allowed the chilled water loop to return to a safe temperature which allowed us to restart the chillers."},{"id":"AZ-AUE-2023:S24","text":"This shutdown of infrastructure resulted in a further reduction of service availability for this Availability Zone."},{"id":"AZ-AUE-2023:S25","text":"The chillers were successfully brought back online at 12:12 UTC, and data hall temperatures returned to operational thresholds by 13:30 UTC."},{"id":"AZ-AUE-2023:S113","text":"Incremental load increases over time in the Availability Zone resulted in a chiller operating configuration that was susceptible to a timing defect in the Chiller Management System."},{"id":"AZ-AUE-2023:S114","text":"We have de-risked this failure to restart due to voltage fluctuations, by implementing a change to the control timing logic on the Chiller Management System (Completed)."},{"id":"AZ-AUE-2023:S115","text":"Emergency Operation Procedure for manual restarts of simultaneous chiller failures has changed from an ‘adjacent’ sequence to a data hall ‘load based’ sequence to ensure all impacted data halls have partial cooling, to slow thermal runaway while full cooling is being restored (Completed)."},{"id":"AZ-AUE-2023:S116","text":"Following this incident, as a temporary mitigation, we increased technician staffing levels at the datacenter to be prepared to execute manual restart procedures of our chillers prior to the change to the Chiller Management System to prevent restart failures."},{"id":"AZ-AUE-2023:S117","text":"Based on our incident analysis the staffing levels at the time would have been sufficient to prevent impact if a ‘load based' chiller restart sequence had been followed, which we have since implemented (Completed)."},{"id":"AZ-AUE-2023:S133","text":"Our incident management team is exploring ways to harden our readiness,
